study_families.study_label: Vitamin D status secondary analysis, placebo arms of acute + 4-week bovine colostrum RCTs, prolonged cycling
study_families.design: p.2978 Design: 'This is a secondary analysis of two randomised controlled trials of nutritional interventions (acute and 4 weeks of bovine colostrum supplementation) and immune responses to prolonged exercise. The participants in this study took part in the control (placebo) arm of these trials'
study_families.training_load: p.2979 Trial procedures: 'During the 48 h preceding the experimental trial, participants were asked to refrain from heavy exercise and alcohol consumption'
study_families.cointerventions: p.2978 Design: 'participants took part in the control (placebo) arm of two RCTs of bovine colostrum supplementation; no active colostrum supplement is analysed in this report'
study_families.study_notes: Single acute exercise bout (2.5 h cycling, 15% Delta) performed by participants drawn from the placebo arms of two parent bovine-colostrum RCTs (ref. 26 and related trial); vitamin D status (deficient vs non-deficient, threshold <33 nmol/L) is a post-hoc observational stratification of this placebo-arm sample, not a randomised factor. Ethics: Aberystwyth University Research Ethics Committee.

reports.title: Vitamin D status modulates innate immune responses and metabolomic profiles following acute prolonged cycling
reports.authors: Jones AW; Mironas A; Mur LAJ; Beckmann M; Thatcher R; Davison G
source_locator: p.2977 header: 'Received: 13 March 2022 / Accepted: 22 May 2023 / Published online: 17 July 2023'
reports.inclusion_reason: Identifiable single acute bout (2.5 h cycling at 15%Delta, ~55-60% VO2max), pre-exercise baseline plus immediate-post and 1h-post samples, generally healthy adult recreationally active males; direct immune-cell/function measures (leukocyte counts, neutrophil degranulation/oxidative burst) plus biofluid (plasma) metabolomics with an explicit immune objective; supplement confound removed because only the placebo arm of parent RCTs is analysed.
reports.reviewer_notes: No provisional exclusion. FT08 (mixed intervention not separable) checked and ruled out: 'This is a secondary analysis of two randomised controlled trials of nutritional interventions (acute and 4 weeks of bovine colostrum supplementation)... The participants in this study took part in the control (placebo) arm of these trials' (p.2978 Design) -- i.e. the active supplement arm is explicitly excluded from this analysis, so the exercise effect analysed here is not confounded by colostrum supplementation.
reports.author_stated_use: p.2988 Discussion/Conclusion: 'supports current advice of monitoring circulating 25(OH)D concentrations and the consideration of sensible sun exposure in summer months or a suitable vitamin D3 supplementation strategy in the winter months'
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.2977 Introduction: 'transient perturbations of cellular and mucosal immunity occurs following prolonged, strenuous exercise (commonly referred to as an 'open window' of immunodepression)'

p.2986 Discussion: 'Blunted blood neutrophil responses to in vitro stimuli are one of the classical measures of the 'open window' period of immune dysfunction following acute prolonged endurance exercise'

cohorts.cohort_label: 23 healthy recreationally active males, placebo-arm of bovine-colostrum RCTs, stratified by plasma 25(OH)D status
cohorts.baseline_health: p.2978 Participants: 'healthy, recreationally active males ... non-smokers and reported no symptoms of infection or consumption of any medication or dietary supplements for 4 weeks prior to commencement of, and during, the study'
cohorts.age_sex: p.2978 Participants: 'Twenty three healthy, recreationally active males (age 25 +/- 7 years; 96% white ethnicity; body mass [BM] 76 +/- 8 kg; height 179 +/- 6 cm; maximal oxygen uptake [VO2max] 56 +/- 9 mL.kg-1.min-1)'
cohorts.training_status: recreationally active (not elite/competitive athletes; not sedentary)
cohorts.sport: NR (general recreationally active; cycling used as the exercise test modality, not necessarily participants' habitual sport)
cohorts.cohort_notes: Deficient (<33 nmol/L 25(OH)D) n=7, non-deficient (>33 nmol/L) n=16 (Abstract/Table 1); same cohort used for blood immune, metabolomic and saliva measures. Saliva antimicrobial-peptide (sLac/sLys) analyses are reduced to n=5 deficient / n=10 non-deficient after excluding 8 participants for blood-contaminated saliva (p.2986-87 Mucosal responses).
cohorts.age_range: NR (mean +/- SD only: 25 +/- 7 years; no explicit minimum/maximum age range or inclusion age threshold stated)

measurements.platform: ELISA (Merck Calbiochem); in vitro bacterial stimulation (S. aureus, P. fluorescens, E. aerogenes)
measurements.comparison: deficient vs non-deficient groups, pre-exercise vs post-exercise vs 1h post-exercise (two-way mixed ANOVA); values expressed as % of pre-exercise
measurements.effect_measure: % of pre-exercise value, group main effect and group x time interaction p-values
measurements.effect_value: main effect of group p=0.010 (lower in deficient); group x time interaction p=0.003; deficient group 1h post-exercise reduction -43% [95% CI -70,-15] vs non-deficient 1% [-20,21] (p=0.003 between-group at 1h); within-deficient-group one-way ANOVA pre-to-1h decrease p=0.007
measurements.effect_unit: % of pre-exercise value; mean difference with 95% CI for the 1h-post comparison
measurements.effect_uncertainty: 95% CI given for the key between-group/within-group contrasts (Abstract; Results Neutrophil responses)
measurements.null_findings: non-deficient group showed no significant main effect of time (one-way ANOVA p=0.383)
measurements.measurement_notes: Direct ex-vivo immune-effector-function measure (neutrophil degranulation), kept distinct from the plasma metabolomics measures per task instruction.

measurements.effect_measure: main-effect and interaction p-values
measurements.effect_value: main effect of time p<0.001 (decrease at post- and 1h-post vs pre, p=0.001); no main effect of group (p=0.857); no group x time interaction (p=0.258)
measurements.effect_uncertainty: exact p-values given, no CI reported for this analyte
measurements.null_findings: no effect of vitamin D group or group x time interaction on PMA-stimulated oxidative burst (explicitly non-significant, p=0.857 and p=0.258)
measurements.measurement_notes: Vitamin-D-independent decline in oxidative burst, contrasted explicitly by the authors with the vitamin-D-dependent elastase/degranulation result (receptor-mediated vs PMA artificial-stimulation pathways, p.2987 Discussion).

eligibility_opinion.rationale: An identifiable single 2.5 h cycling bout at 15% Delta (~55-60% VO2max) with a pre-exercise baseline plus immediate-post and 1h-post samples satisfies Core A (p.2979 Exercise trial procedures/Blood sampling); the exercise effect is not confounded by the parent trials' bovine-colostrum supplement because only the placebo arm is analysed here ('participants in this study took part in the control (placebo) arm of these trials', p.2978 Design), resolving the FT08 mixed-intervention concern. Direct immune-cell counts, ex vivo neutrophil functional assays and biofluid (plasma) metabolomics with an explicit immune-modulation aim ('to suggest how the immune system may be modulated', p.2978 Introduction) both support an eligible immune link; no repeated identified bouts are reported, so Support B does not apply.

unresolved_questions: cohorts.adult_stratum_separable: only mean+/-SD age (25+/-7 y) is reported for the 23 males, with no explicit inclusion-age threshold stated anywhere in Methods; recorded NR rather than inferred as all_participants_adult.

Total tested feature count (tested_universe_n) for the untargeted FIE-MS plasma metabolomics screen is not explicitly stated as a single number in the main text (only scan ranges and post-hoc discriminatory-metabolite counts are given); recorded NR in the assay-universe row (M-R12-016).

Arachidonic acid is reported as significantly elevated across all timepoints in the deficient group (Fig. 4B, narrative text) but, unlike the Table 3 metabolites, no single ANOVA F/P value for AA alone is given in the main text; charted as a reported_result_summary row without a digitized numeric effect value (effect_value_source=reported_main_text_or_table, narrative only) rather than reading the bar/line graph, per the manual's 'use numbers reported in text/tables first' rule.

marker_family vocabulary gap: salivary lactoferrin (sLac) and lysozyme (sLys) are 'recognized immune mediators' (reports.immune_link) but do not fit any specific controlled marker_family value (not mucosal_sIgA, not cytokine_or_inflammatory_mediator, not immunoglobulin_or_complement in the classic sense); charted as marker_family='other' and flagged for the team to consider adding an antimicrobial-peptide/mucosal-AMP category distinct from sIgA.

Whether the linoleic acid-arachidonic acid correlation (r=0.821, p<0.001) and the plasma-25(OH)D-to-elastase-change correlation (r=0.458, p=0.028) should be charted as separate precision_validation 'within_cohort_association' rows at the individual-measurement level (rather than folded into the marker-family-level evidence_notes as done here) is a row-granularity question flagged for team standardisation, parallel to the R42 row-unit question.
